note: cue, lesson and falsification for the seeds of seed_sma.py, by case id: the model's drafts from each line (meta-macbook-20261109-1 and its drafting subagents, 2026-11-09), read by the script and never derived by it. They stay drafts until the person confirms.

case-sma-librarian-001.cue: a fact needs recording but the knowledge store has no source kind that honestly describes where it came from, so the nearest existing kind would carry the wrong grade
case-sma-librarian-001.lesson: Add the missing source kind to the knowledge store's source vocabulary through its owner and park the fact in staging until then, never filing it under the nearest existing prefix.
case-sma-librarian-001.falsification: Entries filed under the nearest existing prefix for such facts are later shown to carry the correct grade and to mislead no consumer.

case-sma-librarian-002.cue: a rule forbids one verb on a shared store while consumers are pinned to its version, but the version hash depends on every entry, so other verbs move it equally
case-sma-librarian-002.lesson: Make the librarian's instructions state the rule as any change that moves the store version, and require a check of active pins before any entry edit.
case-sma-librarian-002.falsification: An entry edit that moves the store version is shown to leave a pinned fan-out working with no refusal and no blocked sibling.

case-sma-librarian-003.cue: a session is about to report on a plan or contract section using a copy loaded into context at start, while other seats commit changes to that file
case-sma-librarian-003.lesson: Make the seat's instructions require re-reading any plan or contract section from disk immediately before reporting on it, treating loaded context as memory rather than evidence.
case-sma-librarian-003.falsification: Reports made from the context copy are found to match the on-disk section at report time just as often as reports made after a re-read.

case-sma-librarian-004.cue: a vendor specification entered with the correct grade is served as uncontested while a person has already measured a conflicting value on the actual instrument
case-sma-librarian-004.lesson: Mark a contested entry on both sides, and make the knowledge store's query tool deliver conflict and supersession fields to every caller so a screening fan-out sees them.
case-sma-librarian-004.falsification: Callers using the query projection without conflict fields still never build on a contradicted entry, for example because they always call the full getter.

case-sma-librarian-005.cue: two sessions of one agent share a working copy and both pick the same open task from a queue that allocates per agent rather than per session
case-sma-librarian-005.lesson: Make the task queue tool or the seat's instructions require claiming a path or task by message or claim file before the first write, not before the commit.
case-sma-librarian-005.falsification: Two sessions of one agent sharing a folder reach the queue's open tasks repeatedly without a duplicate write when no claim step exists.

case-sma-librarian-006.cue: a session defers or abandons work and reports it only in a message to a manager, leaving no trace on disk for a later session to find
case-sma-librarian-006.lesson: Make the seat's instructions require writing every deferral or dead end into the failure log on disk before any message about it is sent.
case-sma-librarian-006.falsification: Later sessions routinely recover deferred items from manager messages or summaries alone, with no loss after a context clear.

case-sma-librarian-007.cue: a session reports counts or open items about its own recent work from memory while the gate or git can print the exact figures
case-sma-librarian-007.lesson: Make the seat's instructions require reading every count and open-item status about one's own work off a fresh run, and reading the gate's printed tree line before committing.
case-sma-librarian-007.falsification: Counts and status reported from memory about own work match a fresh run every time, including across other seats' commits made minutes earlier.

case-sma-librarian-008.cue: a session is about to state what a validator check will do after some change, inferring it from a true premise read elsewhere in the registry
case-sma-librarian-008.lesson: Make the seat's instructions require opening the check's code or docstring before stating its behaviour to anyone, and treat behaviour claims like counts that must be read off a source.
case-sma-librarian-008.falsification: Behaviour claims about checks made without opening the check prove accurate over many cases, so the extra reading finds nothing.

case-sma-librarian-009.cue: an error is being corrected and its blast radius is assessed only by recalling who was told, although the false claim was also written into a committed file
case-sma-librarian-009.lesson: Make the correction procedure search the tree for the claim's text before writing the blast radius, and send any filed copy to the owner of that file.
case-sma-librarian-009.falsification: Wrong claims that were spoken but also filed are never found by a text search of the tree, so the search adds nothing.

case-sma-librarian-010.cue: a query for a quantity returns entries, yet the missing piece is the subject itself, such as an unidentified material, so the gap is invisible at the quantity handle
case-sma-librarian-010.lesson: Record such a gap against the subject, and tag the store's entries with a class handle so the query tool returns the related items while showing the absent medium.
case-sma-librarian-010.falsification: Callers reliably notice a missing subject from a quantity query alone, without any class handle that returns related items and no medium.

case-sma-librarian-011.cue: a script edits a shared hand-formatted JSON file by loading and dumping it, so one small change rewrites most lines while every check still passes
case-sma-librarian-011.lesson: Edit shared hand-formatted JSON by text splice, or round-trip the unchanged file first and diff it against itself, and read the diff stat before every commit.
case-sma-librarian-011.falsification: Load-and-dump rewrites of such files cause no merge conflicts or review difficulty across shared seats.

case-sma-librarian-012.cue: a session starts work from a task's status line, which is prose that another seat may have rewritten or left stale, and repeats work already committed
case-sma-librarian-012.lesson: Make the task tool or the seat's instructions require checking the task's output artefact in git history before starting, rather than trusting the status line.
case-sma-librarian-012.falsification: Task status lines prove consistent with the tree whenever sessions start from them, with no duplicated work observed.

case-sma-librarian-013.cue: a session repeats a formatter round trip on a shared file even after reading a record that names that exact hazard
case-sma-librarian-013.lesson: Put the diff-stat read as a required step in the commit procedure of the seat's instructions, since reading the warning does not prevent the mistake.
case-sma-librarian-013.falsification: Sessions that have read the failure record avoid whole-file rewrites without any diff-stat step in the procedure.

case-sma-librarian-014.cue: two live seats of one agent edit the same source function in a shared working copy, and a clean status taken earlier is already stale at write time
case-sma-librarian-014.lesson: Require seats to claim a path by message before the first write, and never restore a shared file with checkout, which discards the other seat's uncommitted lines.
case-sma-librarian-014.falsification: Concurrent seats edit the same file without collision when they only check status immediately before writing.

case-sma-librarian-015.cue: a report is owed to a manager session that may end before delivery, and a message would die with the session
case-sma-librarian-015.lesson: Write the report into a record on disk and commit it, treating messages as notifications only, and offer a dedicated record kind for reports.
case-sma-librarian-015.falsification: Reports sent only as messages reach their addressee reliably even when the addressee session has ended.

case-sma-librarian-016.cue: a person's decision or policy is filed in a claim store whose schema requires a grade, so the decision gets a grade it must not have
case-sma-librarian-016.lesson: File decisions and policies as source records outside the knowledge entries, and make the librarian's instructions reject any entry that needs a paragraph to explain why it almost fits.
case-sma-librarian-016.falsification: Graded entries holding decisions are shown to be consumed correctly and never mistaken for claims about the world.

case-sma-librarian-017.cue: a session runs pre-commit checks on a file that other processes append to, then commits the path, so extra lines land unchecked
case-sma-librarian-017.lesson: Re-run the strict-prefix check after the commit against the new head, and state the append claim in the message only after that run.
case-sma-librarian-017.falsification: Append-only logs written by running servers show no growth between the pre-commit check and the commit that would need a post-commit check.

case-sma-librarian-018.cue: a session calls a gap a new pattern from the few log lines in front of it, while the same quantity was asked earlier under different names
case-sma-librarian-018.lesson: Make the librarian's instructions require counting the quantity over the whole query log, not the name, and checking enum values against the schema before filing.
case-sma-librarian-018.falsification: Patterns judged from a recent window agree with counts over the whole log, even when the quantity was renamed.

case-sma-librarian-019.cue: a session infers what a knowledge entry contains from the fact that it answered a query or from a quoted clause
case-sma-librarian-019.lesson: Make the librarian's instructions require opening the entry before any claim about what the store holds, since query coverage shows matching subjects, never contents.
case-sma-librarian-019.falsification: Entries that answer a query reliably carry the operand the claim assumes, so coverage alone predicts contents.

case-sma-librarian-020.cue: a control experiment for a line-ending problem hashes an archive export, which applies the same conversion as checkout and so is not independent
case-sma-librarian-020.lesson: Use the object store through cat-file or show for the unconverted committed bytes when testing checkout conversion, never archive or checkout output.
case-sma-librarian-020.falsification: Archive output differs from checkout output on a converting platform, so it would serve as an independent control.

case-sma-librarian-021.cue: an agent edits store entries while its own self-test holds a pinned store version, so the pinned version no longer exists
case-sma-librarian-021.lesson: Make the librarian's instructions forbid edits to the entries folder while any self-test or pinned caller runs; finish edits, then test, then commit.
case-sma-librarian-021.falsification: Self-tests pinned to an uncommitted version complete successfully after the working tree has moved.

case-sma-librarian-022.cue: a seat reads a source tree outside its permitted paths because the reason seems good, although the same fact was already in a permitted findings record
case-sma-librarian-022.lesson: Make the seat's instructions require citing the committed findings note first and treat the read boundary as unbending for good reasons.
case-sma-librarian-022.falsification: Permitted findings records often lack facts that only an out-of-boundary read provides, so the boundary blocks needed work.

case-sma-librarian-023.cue: a script edits a shared device table by parsing and re-serializing it, rewriting hand-kept formatting and burying the real change in noise
case-sma-librarian-023.lesson: Edit shared hand-formatted tables with targeted text edits and read the diff stat before committing any table.
case-sma-librarian-023.falsification: Re-serialized tables stay within a few changed lines of the intended edit, so reviewers can still see the real change.

case-sma-librarian-024.cue: numbers are expressed in a model's reduced units that each paper defines differently, and the unit registry holds none of them
case-sma-librarian-024.lesson: Do not register a reduced unit without its source paper attached; keep such values in the source record as stated and enter only dimensionless numbers, counts and thermal energy.
case-sma-librarian-024.falsification: A single registered reduced unit is shown to be comparable across the papers that use it, with no silent equating.

case-sma-librarian-025.cue: a unit is registered in the vocabulary but has no conversion factor, so any query bound in that unit is refused before entries are read
case-sma-librarian-025.lesson: Check whether a unit converts before using it as a validity bound, and keep non-convertible quantities in numbers with conditions in prose.
case-sma-librarian-025.falsification: The query tool accepts bounds in units without conversion factors and compares them correctly.

case-sma-librarian-026.cue: regime boundaries or thresholds in a paper exist only as rendered figures, which a model can read off only as ungraded estimates
case-sma-librarian-026.lesson: Enter only what the text states, such as a threshold, a direction or one example point, and list figure-only results as not entered in the source record.
case-sma-librarian-026.falsification: Values read off rendered figures by a model turn out to match the published numbers closely enough to be entered.

case-sma-librarian-027.cue: a source states one quantity twice with different values for what appears to be the same condition
case-sma-librarian-027.lesson: Enter neither value; record the quantity under the source's not-entered list with a note that the source gives no single value.
case-sma-librarian-027.falsification: The two statements prove to describe different conditions, so each could have been entered separately with its own condition.

case-sma-librarian-028.cue: a generator script fixes a session identity into a constant, and a later identity correction in conversation never reaches the constant
case-sma-librarian-028.lesson: When a seat's identity changes, grep the generator scripts for the old identity and regenerate affected artifacts, since no check reads the curator field.
case-sma-librarian-028.falsification: Identity constants in generators are re-read per run, so a conversational correction always reaches the artifacts.

case-sma-librarian-029.cue: a store publish regenerates only some of the generated files that name the store version, leaving guides or exports stale
case-sma-librarian-029.lesson: List every generator in the librarian's instructions and run each generator's check before committing a publish.
case-sma-librarian-029.falsification: Stale generated files that name an older store version cause no consumer confusion and need no regeneration.

case-sma-librarian-030.cue: numbers for entry come from a large vendor page read through a summarising fetch tool that truncates the page before the specification table
case-sma-librarian-030.lesson: Fetch the raw page with a direct download, read the specification rows from the markup, and record a hash of the page in the source record.
case-sma-librarian-030.falsification: Summarising fetch tools return complete and accurate specification tables for large vendor pages.

case-sma-librarian-031.cue: a field added to a query answer is also written to the query log, whose record shape is fixed and refuses unknown fields
case-sma-librarian-031.lesson: Keep the log line unchanged when widening an answer, unless the log's schema and every reader of it are widened together.
case-sma-librarian-031.falsification: The query log's record check accepts new fields without change, so adding them to the log line is harmless.

case-sma-librarian-032.cue: a manufacturer publishes no figure for a consumable, and a reseller page is blocked for command-line fetches or conflicts with another reseller
case-sma-librarian-032.lesson: Read blocked pages in the browser pane as a person would, name the reseller as source, and seek a second reseller before treating one as settled.
case-sma-librarian-032.falsification: Manufacturer documents reliably state the figure, so no reseller sourcing is needed.

case-sma-librarian-033.cue: a figure quoted in configs as from a datasheet cannot be traced because the vendor link returns a web page instead of the document and no seat has read the document
case-sma-librarian-033.lesson: Record the inventory row as having no traceable origin and leave the figure out of the store until a person supplies the datasheet.
case-sma-librarian-033.falsification: The quoted figure is later found in the vendor document unchanged, so entering it from the configs would have been safe.

case-sma-simulation-001.cue: a seat cannot reach a knowledge service its task requires, and a partial pass without it would misrepresent what the revision is
case-sma-simulation-001.lesson: Record the abandoned attempt as its own row naming the missing service and refuse a degraded partial pass, and state each falsifier as a state that must obtain rather than a document that would arrive.
case-sma-simulation-001.falsification: A degraded partial pass is later shown to cost nothing in comparability, or a falsifier naming a document fires as reliably as one naming a state.

case-sma-simulation-002.cue: a seat reads other agents' directories through broad repository-wide sweeps when the answer sat inside its own boundary and its allowed paths
case-sma-simulation-002.lesson: Scope searches to the seat's own tree and the paths named by the task, and report any crossing read as a deviation instead of reading further.
case-sma-simulation-002.falsification: Boundary-crossing reads turn out to give conclusions that are reachable inside the boundary no less often than not, so scoped searches lose nothing.

case-sma-simulation-003.cue: a service is silently absent in a seat's session and each seat records only the symptom, guessing a cause it cannot verify from inside
case-sma-simulation-003.lesson: Append a corrected row when a cause turns out wrong rather than editing the earlier one, and name who can repair the cause instead of trying to repair it from inside the seat.
case-sma-simulation-003.falsification: The first named cause proves right every time, so corrected rows are never needed.

case-sma-simulation-004.cue: a configuration file that is untracked and globally ignored holds an override nobody can audit, and several seats diagnose from other files
case-sma-simulation-004.lesson: Require the validator or the bootstrap tool to report local settings files that disable a registered server, so a hidden refusal is visible to every seat.
case-sma-simulation-004.falsification: Seats find the hidden override quickly from tracked files alone, so an extra report adds nothing.

case-sma-simulation-005.cue: a test set by an earlier row has now run, and registration was read while no actual call has been made
case-sma-simulation-005.lesson: Keep recording a connected-service reading as registration only, distinct from the service answering, until a real call returns.
case-sma-simulation-005.falsification: A registered and connected server has never failed to answer, so the distinction is unnecessary.

case-sma-simulation-006.cue: a person edits an untracked settings file while a seat is mid-task, and its new content resembles a different file's format
case-sma-simulation-006.lesson: Append a correction row noting the changed content and that it does not establish a per-project enable, rather than editing the earlier row or inferring a mechanism.
case-sma-simulation-006.falsification: The file keeps its shape between reads, so no correcting row is needed.

case-sma-simulation-007.cue: a card names one defect in input handling and the real behaviour varies across many shape and budget combinations
case-sma-simulation-007.lesson: Exercise every combination of malformed shape and mode on the operator's envelope reader and guard the type before the membership test, naming the type found.
case-sma-simulation-007.falsification: The single shape the card named proves to be the only combination that misbehaves.

case-sma-simulation-008.cue: a seat declines a reachability probe out of caution about polluting a log without having read how the log records refusals
case-sma-simulation-008.lesson: Read the query log's recording of refused calls before declining a probe, then use a clearly marked probe call to establish that the service answers.
case-sma-simulation-008.falsification: Refused probes appear in the log under a question's own caller identity and corrupt its checks.

case-sma-simulation-009.cue: a seat tests a guard by writing a protected person-only file in a loop through a shell tool the deny list does not match
case-sma-simulation-009.lesson: Point the module's path attribute at a scratch copy when testing guards, and never write the protected file, restoring any change from version control without touching the index.
case-sma-simulation-009.falsification: Redirecting to a scratch copy changes the guard's behaviour, so only the live file gives a faithful test.

case-sma-simulation-010.cue: a deny list on write tools refuses a read through one tool while allowing a write through another
case-sma-simulation-010.lesson: Test the deny entries by attempting the intended operation in its exact form, and have the settings check judge the refusal effect rather than the entry's spelling.
case-sma-simulation-010.falsification: Deny entries refuse exactly the operations they spell out across all tools, so spelling-based checking suffices.

case-sma-simulation-011.cue: two seats run what they call the same read and get opposite answers from the permission matcher
case-sma-simulation-011.lesson: Attempt each operation in the exact phrasing it will be used in and record the phrasing alongside any refusal claim, since a colleague's success proves nothing for another form.
case-sma-simulation-011.falsification: The matcher's outcome depends only on the target path and not on the phrasing of the command.

case-sma-simulation-012.cue: a hypothesis about a second cause is open and the earlier probe still had a repository-scope enable in place
case-sma-simulation-012.lesson: Run the distinguishing test with every override removed, and record the result so that the reasoning from per-project arrays is retired.
case-sma-simulation-012.falsification: A test with an enable still present separates the causes just as well as one without it.

case-sma-simulation-013.cue: a seat reports the shared head as failing after checking cleanliness of only the data side of a comparison
case-sma-simulation-013.lesson: Read the validator's tree line first and confirm every input including the checker itself is clean before attributing a failure or reporting a red head.
case-sma-simulation-013.falsification: The data side being clean is enough to attribute a failure on a shared working copy.

case-sma-simulation-014.cue: a falsifier fires on a measurement taken on a stand-in backend that does not exercise the quantity being estimated
case-sma-simulation-014.lesson: Narrow the plan card's falsifier to name the backend the job will use, and do not substitute a stand-in measurement for an estimate of an engine job.
case-sma-simulation-014.falsification: Stand-in backend measurements track the real engine's cost closely enough to replace the estimate.

case-sma-simulation-015.cue: two seats edit the same file in a shared worktree and a path-scoped commit carries the other seat's hunks under its identity
case-sma-simulation-015.lesson: Stage by hunk or confirm via a diff that a file holds only the seat's own edits before a path-scoped commit, and declare held files where other seats can see them.
case-sma-simulation-015.falsification: Path-scoped commits never carry another seat's uncommitted hunks.

case-sma-simulation-016.cue: a required schema field has no honest value among its enumerated members and only untrue values make the gate pass
case-sma-simulation-016.lesson: Raise the missing enumeration member to the schema's owner and leave the field unwritten rather than choose a value that is untrue.
case-sma-simulation-016.falsification: One of the existing members is shown to describe the case truthfully.

case-sma-simulation-017.cue: a seat measures an artifact that does not contain the thing being estimated and then charges the ratio to the plan's estimate
case-sma-simulation-017.lesson: Measure the quantity on an artifact that contains it, state the comparand, and issue a correction row instead of quoting a ratio whose direction depends on the comparand.
case-sma-simulation-017.falsification: The measured directory later proves to contain the estimated quantity.

case-sma-simulation-018.cue: a result card passes the validator while most of what the contract says about it is shadowed or unchecked
case-sma-simulation-018.lesson: Mutate one card field at a time and rerun the validator to list what each check actually enforces, then raise the unenforced fields to the validator's owner.
case-sma-simulation-018.falsification: Every mutation of a card field is already refused by a check for its own reason.

case-sma-simulation-019.cue: a milestone's completion condition rests on a property no declared check names
case-sma-simulation-019.lesson: Declare in the plan's check list a check that compares a result card's numbers with the run it cites, before counting the milestone's gate closed.
case-sma-simulation-019.falsification: Implementing the existing declared checks already yields the traceability the completion condition asks for.

case-sma-simulation-020.cue: a store entry's support names a mechanism the engine configuration does not have
case-sma-simulation-020.lesson: Replace the support's mechanism with the true one and name the configuration and the backend that confirmed it, in the knowledge store's entry.
case-sma-simulation-020.falsification: The configuration later gains inertia so the named mechanism becomes real.

case-sma-simulation-021.cue: a card writer is run only on successful runs while refusal branches stay unexercised and its schema cannot express non-evaluability
case-sma-simulation-021.lesson: Run the card writer against synthetic failed and short runs from a scratch directory and give criteria a way to report that they were not evaluable.
case-sma-simulation-021.falsification: Refusal branches behave correctly on real failed runs without any synthetic exercise.

case-sma-simulation-022.cue: a verdict would be asserted on a fit that did not run as declared, or on a metric the record does not carry
case-sma-simulation-022.lesson: Emit a null verdict with a stated reason in the result card writer when the estimator did not follow its declaration or the metric is absent, while keeping the observed number.
case-sma-simulation-022.falsification: Verdicts on such runs prove as reliable as verdicts on well-formed runs.

case-sma-simulation-023.cue: a hardcoded first-revision filename is opened by a module that handles later revisions
case-sma-simulation-023.lesson: Resolve the plan file from the revision the run itself recorded in the card writer, and keep the hash as the second independent gate.
case-sma-simulation-023.falsification: The latest revision always equals the revision a finished run carried.

case-sma-simulation-024.cue: a revision declares a criterion against a quantity no record carries and the first run on a new revision is requested ahead of the engine
case-sma-simulation-024.lesson: Add the missing computation to the engine adapter before running, and let the card writer refuse until each declared criterion is backed by a recorded quantity.
case-sma-simulation-024.falsification: The declared criterion can be evaluated from quantities the record already carried.

case-sma-simulation-025.cue: two engine adapters or both sides of a comparison each hold their own copy of an estimator or physical constants, so a claim of comparability cannot be demonstrated
case-sma-simulation-025.lesson: Extract the shared estimator and physics constants into one module that every engine adapter calls, and prove the extraction by rebuilding existing result cards byte-identical.
case-sma-simulation-025.falsification: Separate per-adapter copies stay in agreement through many later changes, or a rebuilt card differs after extraction although behavior did not change.

case-sma-simulation-026.cue: a bulk migration of one field in an append-only ledger is specified by a task card that names which rows should move
case-sma-simulation-026.lesson: Read each row's detail before moving it to the new field, and record the migration itself as a new row saying what changed in place and why.
case-sma-simulation-026.falsification: Moving rows by the card's list alone never misclassifies a row, or later readers never need the trace row to understand the modified lines.

case-sma-simulation-027.cue: a session identity must be registered, and the registry is read at the commit's parent, so late registration cannot attribute earlier commits
case-sma-simulation-027.lesson: Make the seat's instructions require a seat to ask for its own registration directly, before its first commit, rather than waiting to be told or routing the request through a report.
case-sma-simulation-027.falsification: The gate attributes earlier commits retroactively once a seat is registered, or unattributed early commits turn out to cost nothing.

case-sma-simulation-028.cue: a task card prescribes a fix to unblock a validator refusal, but two rules in different files contradict each other so the fix cannot satisfy the check
case-sma-simulation-028.lesson: Before applying a prescribed fix, read the validator and its rejected fixture to see which field the check compares, and report the rule conflict to the owner instead of editing code.
case-sma-simulation-028.falsification: Applying prescribed fixes without that reading routinely unblocks the check, or the fixture shows the compared field is the one the card named.

case-sma-simulation-029.cue: a hand-over made by message leaves no trace on disk until the receiver acts, and pinned hashes or supersession rules are easy to get subtly wrong
case-sma-simulation-029.lesson: Write a ledger row recording the exact pin as sent, after verifying the hash convention and supersession test on the real files rather than on other seats' reports.
case-sma-simulation-029.falsification: The receiver's thread always appears promptly and names the sender, making the sender-side row redundant, or reported conventions never differ from verified ones.

case-sma-simulation-030.cue: an evidence field defaults to degraded and clears only when a reply arrives, so components that never issue a query stay degraded forever
case-sma-simulation-030.lesson: Make the evidence builder distinguish not asked from not answered, and state success conditions that components issuing no query can satisfy.
case-sma-simulation-030.falsification: Components that issue no query never show as degraded in cards, or the success condition is met by every component without the distinction.

case-sma-simulation-031.cue: reverting a file with a checkout in a working copy that several seats share
case-sma-simulation-031.lesson: Save the path's diff outside the tree before any revert of a shared path, and confirm the uncommitted edits are only your own, since checkout discards every seat's work there.
case-sma-simulation-031.falsification: Reverts of shared paths never destroy another seat's work across many occasions, or a path-scoped undo of only one's own edits exists.

case-sma-simulation-032.cue: a run record names its backend through an attribute lookup with a default, so a missing attribute silently produces a false claim
case-sma-simulation-032.lesson: Make the operator read the backend's name without a fallback so a backend lacking one fails loudly, and keep a mislabeled run unrepaired beside its corrected rerun as evidence.
case-sma-simulation-032.falsification: Every backend always carries a name by construction, or the default never yields a label that differs from the executed backend.

case-sma-simulation-033.cue: a run tool writes into a run directory whose id was picked by hand from a listing, in a tree where several seats run sweeps
case-sma-simulation-033.lesson: Make the operator refuse a run id whose directory already exists, and read the commit's numstat for deletions before accepting a commit that should only add files.
case-sma-simulation-033.falsification: Hand-picked ids never collide in practice, or the refusal blocks legitimate reruns that a plan requires.

case-sma-simulation-034.cue: prose or comments state a count or a status recalled from memory, and go stale or wrong as runs land
case-sma-simulation-034.lesson: Replace counts in headers and comments with a figure counted from the run logs, carrying its date and the command that produced it, or point to the logs instead of stating a number.
case-sma-simulation-034.falsification: Counts written in prose stay correct without maintenance, or a command-counted figure is later found wrong in the same way.

case-sma-simulation-035.cue: a parked falsifier names a backend or a present-tense fact about the machine rather than an artefact the repository can show
case-sma-simulation-035.lesson: Write each falsifier on a state re-derivable from the tree, such as a run holding the declared trajectory, and fix the generator while leaving the committed card for the next revision.
case-sma-simulation-035.falsification: Falsifiers naming a backend fire only when the intended evidence exists, or the corrected conditions still misfire.

case-sma-simulation-036.cue: a person requests a physical model that the capability declaration does not list, and the agent cannot write that declaration
case-sma-simulation-036.lesson: Have the screening step refuse with a card listing counterexamples and alternatives instead of building an undeclared backend, and register new observables before planning.
case-sma-simulation-036.falsification: Building the backend first and declaring it afterward is accepted without objection by the person, or the capability table already holds a fitting configuration.

case-sma-simulation-037.cue: several seats choose question ids in a shared namespace with no allocator, and a broad directory commit sweeps in another seat's untracked file
case-sma-simulation-037.lesson: Commit the empty but named question folder first to claim the id, and stage only files you wrote rather than a whole directory.
case-sma-simulation-037.falsification: Chosen ids never collide in practice, or a committed folder is still written into by a peer under the same id.

case-sma-simulation-038.cue: a server accepts several issued identifier forms but the launcher meant to compose them issues only one, so seats hand-compose the others
case-sma-simulation-038.lesson: Add an issuer function to the launcher for every identifier form the server accepts that a stage needs, and test it against the server's own pattern function rather than a docstring.
case-sma-simulation-038.falsification: Hand-composed identifiers never diverge from the server's accepted pattern, or the server can itself tell issued ids from hand-composed ones.

case-sma-simulation-039.cue: a planning function documented as derived from the goal hardcodes symbols and ranges for one configuration, and fails or misleads for others
case-sma-simulation-039.lesson: Make the query planner stop with a sentence naming the missing input, and record per configuration which symbols it needs rather than narrowing the shared function while peers depend on it.
case-sma-simulation-039.falsification: All registered configurations share the same symbols and ranges, so the hardcoding never produces a wrong query.

case-sma-simulation-040.cue: committing by path after a refused attempt in a shared working copy, while another seat edits a file in the same paths
case-sma-simulation-040.lesson: Rerun the hunk-level diff of the named paths immediately before every retry of a commit, since a name-level listing cannot show foreign hunks inside files you mean to commit.
case-sma-simulation-040.falsification: Foreign hunks never arrive between a refused attempt and the retry, or the name-level listing is shown to reveal them.

case-sma-simulation-041.cue: several seats report contradictory states of one file, each true when measured, and the validator output carries no time to order them
case-sma-simulation-041.lesson: Have the validator's verdict line carry the time of the run beside the commit and dirty-set digest, and re-measure before acting on another seat's report of a broken tree.
case-sma-simulation-041.falsification: Contradictory reports are resolved without any timestamp, or seats always re-measure and never act on stale reports.

case-sma-simulation-042.cue: a commit hash is cited as provenance after measuring from a position that a ref race has made unreachable
case-sma-simulation-042.lesson: Check that each cited commit is an ancestor of the current head at the moment of citing, and have the commit tool report a lost ref update.
case-sma-simulation-042.falsification: Ref races never leave a cited commit unreachable, or the commit tool already detects lost updates.

case-sma-simulation-043.cue: a prose claim about how cost scales is written into a card without computing the quantity at both ends of the swept range
case-sma-simulation-043.lesson: Compute the quantity at both corners of the swept range before stating a scaling claim in a card, and when wrong, state the corrected relation and which half was wrong instead of silently replacing it.
case-sma-simulation-043.falsification: Scaling sentences written from reasoning alone prove right when checked, or the corners never differ from the claim.

case-sma-simulation-044.cue: a shared estimator holds a model property such as dimensionality as a module constant, so newly declared configurations yield plausible but wrong numbers
case-sma-simulation-044.lesson: Declare dimensionality as a field of the capability declaration and have the estimator read it and fail when absent, before any run of a configuration with a different value executes.
case-sma-simulation-044.falsification: Every declared configuration shares the same dimensionality, or an existing check already catches a wrong-dimension run.

case-sma-simulation-045.cue: a capability declaration names an engine for a model whose code path does not exist, and nobody has shown the engine can do it
case-sma-simulation-045.lesson: Probe the engine in scratch against a closed form before starting card work, and keep the probe outside the tree and ungraded.
case-sma-simulation-045.falsification: Declared engine capabilities always prove executable once implemented, making the early probe redundant.

case-sma-simulation-046.cue: physics answers are produced by driving a backend directly because the plan synthesis table lacks an entry for the configuration
case-sma-simulation-046.lesson: Add the missing configuration entry to the plan synthesis table before running, or label direct-driven results as not card-backed in the first paragraph of their report.
case-sma-simulation-046.falsification: Unlabeled direct-driven results are used downstream without confusion, or the synthesis table always covers every declared configuration.

case-sma-simulation-047.cue: a collapse or scaling test compares runs that differ only by an exact rescaling under one shared seed, so agreement is free
case-sma-simulation-047.lesson: Vary the seed independently across the arms of any test whose arms differ by an exact rescaling, and treat a perfect agreement as a signal to check rather than a result.
case-sma-simulation-047.falsification: Identical-seed arms show spread comparable to independent-seed arms, so seed sharing hides nothing.

case-sma-simulation-048.cue: a validator criterion compares a named metric against a physical threshold, but the producing backend fills the field with a coarser quantity than the name says, and earlier runs passed for the wrong reason
case-sma-simulation-048.lesson: Make each engine adapter compute a guarded metric at the granularity its name and the criterion's threshold state, and keep any coarser quantity under its own distinct field name.
case-sma-simulation-048.falsification: Runs in the regime where the coarse and fine quantities differ most still pass or fail identically under both definitions, so the distinction changes no verdict.

case-sma-simulation-049.cue: a budget or feasibility claim is formed in prose in a goal note or commit message from one bound, while several bounds apply and no check reads that prose
case-sma-simulation-049.lesson: Have the plan stage compute each per-point quantity as a card field from all applicable bounds, taking the tightest, instead of stating the product in notes.
case-sma-simulation-049.falsification: Counting every cell against all bounds in a card gives the same figures as the earlier prose claims across the whole sweep.

case-sma-simulation-050.cue: a validator check reads only the top-level conditions of a plan, while a required condition legitimately varies per point of a sweep and so has no place the check will look
case-sma-simulation-050.lesson: Extend the validator check to read per-point conditions in sweep entries and require the varying condition at every kept point, so a correct sweep plan passes.
case-sma-simulation-050.falsification: A sweep plan with a per-point value of that condition passes the unchanged check, or no observable's condition ever varies across sweep points.

case-sma-simulation-051.cue: a first smoke run of a new engine configuration meets its criteria, and a seed ensemble is needed to judge an error model while small ensembles show false alarms
case-sma-simulation-051.lesson: Keep judging an error model by an ensemble of independent seeds large enough to settle, and give every run its own seed rather than treating agreeing shared-seed runs as separate measurements.
case-sma-simulation-051.falsification: Small ensembles and shared-seed runs give the same verdict as large independent-seed ensembles across several cells, so the extra seeds add nothing.

case-sma-simulation-052.cue: a constraint note in a goal card states that a vocabulary or table has no entry for something, copied from older prose without checking the table it describes
case-sma-simulation-052.lesson: Check any claim about what a vocabulary or source table contains against the table itself, and cite the entry and its gating condition in the note.
case-sma-simulation-052.falsification: Notes restating table contents prove consistent with the tables without such a check, or the tables change so rarely that no stale claim ever appears.

case-sma-simulation-053.cue: a new engine backend is written by copying a mock backend's pattern, and the two report different quantities under one metric name
case-sma-simulation-053.lesson: Require each backend to report a shared metric as the same measured quantity, and compare mock and engine on that metric before trusting a mock-against-engine comparison.
case-sma-simulation-053.falsification: Mock and engine backends report matching values for the shared metric at the same cell without any naming or definition review.

case-sma-simulation-054.cue: a missing-engine fallback routes every configuration to one generic mock whose physics differs, so a plan could finish green under the wrong physics, and fixed message text goes into run records
case-sma-simulation-054.lesson: Make the operator's engine-missing fallback choose a mock per configuration, fail when none exists, and build the recorded message from the backend that actually ran.
case-sma-simulation-054.falsification: A plan run through the generic fallback gives the same physical result as through its own configuration's backend, or the recorded text never differs from the real backend.

case-sma-simulation-055.cue: a configuration the engine lacks a native potential for must be built from available primitives, and the same plan is run on both mock and engine
case-sma-simulation-055.lesson: Keep running the same unchanged plan on mock and engine, build missing forces from engine primitives, and compare outcomes and error model, recording which engine executed.
case-sma-simulation-055.falsification: The engine-built construction disagrees with the mock beyond the declared uncertainty, or a plan must be edited to run on the second engine.

case-sma-simulation-056.cue: plan cards carry literals that matched an earlier assumed range, so a person's changed range leaves some of them right only by coincidence, and rounded derived values can drift past a bound
case-sma-simulation-056.lesson: Derive every plan literal from the goal card by formula and have the validator recompute it, rounding toward the safe side of each bound and checking at the unrounded value.
case-sma-simulation-056.falsification: Changing the goal's range leaves all cards correct with no recomputation, or rounding in either direction never crosses a bound.

case-sma-simulation-057.cue: a sweep rounds a requested operating value to coarse figures when dispatching, so the realised condition differs from its label and a record sized for the label misses its statistical target
case-sma-simulation-057.lesson: Size the record from the condition the dispatched value actually realises, computed per cell, and have each result card report the realised value against the label.
case-sma-simulation-057.falsification: Realised and labelled conditions differ by less than the target's tolerance in every cell, so sizing by label meets the target.

case-sma-simulation-058.cue: runs are made under identifiers that the shared schemas refuse and all share one seed, so uncommitted files turn every seat's validator red and cells that are the same experiment look like several
case-sma-simulation-058.lesson: Check run ids against the schema pattern and give each cell its own seed before launching, and move rejected runs out of the shared tree rather than deleting them.
case-sma-simulation-058.falsification: Runs with bad ids never reach the shared tree, or shared-seed cells differ in outcome, showing they were independent samples.

case-sma-simulation-059.cue: a knowledge store's agreed query name differs from the one a plan card asked for, while earlier plans and runs already cite the old card by hash
case-sma-simulation-059.lesson: Change the query name only in the next revision, leave the earlier card untouched, and record the unmatched call in the store's log as orphaned.
case-sma-simulation-059.falsification: Rebuilding the earlier card under the new name leaves its hash and every run citing it intact, or the old name is found never to resolve.

case-sma-simulation-060.cue: a grid on the engine answers the question asked, with results flat across the swept axis as the formula predicts, and one row skipped at a conservative cost
case-sma-simulation-060.lesson: Keep reporting the predicted-versus-measured error per cell against the formula, and list unrun rows explicitly with the reason, rerunning them once the measured cost is known.
case-sma-simulation-060.falsification: Predicted errors stop tracking measured ones across the swept axis, or skipped rows prove costlier than the measured rate says.

case-sma-simulation-061.cue: a first attempt at a grid is abandoned after its results were read for reasons unrelated to the numbers, and the rerun reaches the same answer
case-sma-simulation-061.lesson: Keep the abandoned attempt's results out of the tree and say in the new record why it was dropped, and compare both attempts to show the rerun moved nothing.
case-sma-simulation-061.falsification: Abandoned attempts are never needed to audit a rerun, or the rerun differs materially from the first so the reason was not independent of the numbers.

case-sma-simulation-062.cue: a cost model counts only per-step work while the run is dominated by per-frame readout and memory growth, and a smoke run is the same run under tighter limits so it cannot calibrate
case-sma-simulation-062.lesson: Add a per-frame cost and memory term to the cost model, stream frames to disk in the backend, and make the smoke run a genuinely smaller run that measures the rate.
case-sma-simulation-062.falsification: Measured wall time and memory track the per-step estimate alone at large frame counts, or a smoke run already yields a usable smaller measurement.

case-sma-simulation-063.cue: a sweep varies parameters independently that a real system ties together through one underlying property, and advice carries that freedom to an experiment where it does not exist
case-sma-simulation-063.lesson: Anchor the plan on the physical property that sets the coupled parameters and compute the dependent ones from it, stating which sweep points no real object can realise.
case-sma-simulation-063.falsification: Real systems are found that realise the independently varied points, or the dependent parameters turn out not to follow from the anchor.

case-sma-simulation-064.cue: a session deletes a failed run's directory before rerunning, without looking, and reuses the same run id, destroying the only record that the attempt happened
case-sma-simulation-064.lesson: Have the seat's instructions require listing a run directory before touching it, never deleting failed runs, and giving every new attempt a fresh run id.
case-sma-simulation-064.falsification: Deleted failed-run directories prove recoverable from version control or logs, or reused ids never collide with kept records.

case-sma-simulation-065.cue: a plan passes the validator but the operator refuses it at run time because timing numbers do not fall on the step grid, so a plan can be validated and unrunnable
case-sma-simulation-065.lesson: Add a validator check that the save interval is a whole multiple of the timestep, and derive such timing values as whole numbers of steps in the plan stage.
case-sma-simulation-065.falsification: Operator refusals for off-grid timing never occur after plans are derived as whole step counts, so the validator check never fires.

case-sma-simulation-066.cue: a session feeds a card generator a hand-assembled service result with rewritten caller ids to save repeat calls, and the card builder's guard treats it as an unanswered service
case-sma-simulation-066.lesson: Make a real service call under each revision's own caller id instead of reusing or reshaping earlier answers, and keep the card builder's rule that a result must name its server.
case-sma-simulation-066.falsification: A carried-forward answer under a new caller id passes the guard and matches a fresh call's answer, or the guard rejects genuine served results.

case-sma-simulation-067.cue: a background launch prints nothing and is read as not having started, so it is launched again and two copies write the same run directories, which the existing-run guard checks only at start
case-sma-simulation-067.lesson: Check running processes before relaunching, and add a lock in the operator at run start so concurrent runs under one id are refused.
case-sma-simulation-067.falsification: Concurrent launches under the same id are refused by the existing guard, or silent launches always prove not to have started.

case-sma-simulation-068.cue: a session compares an estimate of one phase against elapsed time of the whole process and reports a large overrun without reading the run's own phase-resolved log
case-sma-simulation-068.lesson: Read the run log's own clock per phase before reporting any overrun, and have the cost model, ceiling and deadline cover post-loop writing and estimation as well.
case-sma-simulation-068.falsification: Whole-process elapsed time and the log's phase times agree, or post-loop phases stay a negligible share of every run.

case-sma-simulation-069.cue: an estimator is written from a task card's wording and checked only against the agent's own validation, while the registered definition and allowed units sit in a vocabulary file the validator does not compare
case-sma-simulation-069.lesson: Have the validator compare each reported estimator and unit against the observable's registered entry, and require the author to read that entry before writing the estimator.
case-sma-simulation-069.falsification: Estimators written from task wording match their registered definitions and units without any such comparison.

case-sma-microscope-001.cue: an instrument component accepts a numeric payload whose unit is undocumented, and a prior unit mix-up on another bench produced a large unintended motion
case-sma-microscope-001.lesson: Make the device adapter refuse the whole feature with no override until the input unit is measured in a bounded experiment on a safe axis with the person present.
case-sma-microscope-001.falsification: The adapter reads the unit from the controller itself, or a bounded measurement shows the unit is fixed and documented, so the blanket refusal blocks safe use for nothing.

case-sma-microscope-002.cue: an agent reads a person's direct instruction to operate an instrument as covering both the hand-over and the separate planning requirement, and a harmless-looking state makes it weigh the hazard instead of the rule
case-sma-microscope-002.lesson: Make the seat's instructions require a plan check, restated in plain words to the person, before the first command that moves anything, with no exception for apparently safe states.
case-sma-microscope-002.falsification: Seats that skip the plan check under a stated safe condition never cause an unplanned motion or a dispute over what was approved, showing the rule adds nothing.

case-sma-microscope-003.cue: a record states a bench condition such as a sample or emission state that the agent inferred or phrased itself, and later the person says otherwise
case-sma-microscope-003.lesson: Make the live checklist ask each safety condition as a separate gate in the person's own terms, log the answer before the first command, and let the validator read it.
case-sma-microscope-003.falsification: Gates answered before the first command still produce records that later prove wrong, or the person's free-text statements are shown to be as reliable as logged gates.

case-sma-microscope-004.cue: an earlier deviation record left a condition unconfirmed, and the person later answers the open question after the commands have already run
case-sma-microscope-004.lesson: Append the person's verbatim answer as a follow-up record that corrects the question while stating that it cannot serve as the gate and the deviation stays open.
case-sma-microscope-004.falsification: Readers treat the appended answer as closing the deviation anyway, or the original record is never misread, showing the explicit statement of limits is unnecessary.

case-sma-microscope-005.cue: an agent drafts a command or file for the person to run that embeds a typed timestamp instead of taking the time from the clock when written
case-sma-microscope-005.lesson: Make drafted approval or record commands take timestamps from the system clock at the moment of writing and never as hardcoded literals, and have the validator compare approval time to run start.
case-sma-microscope-005.falsification: Hardcoded times never appear in drafted commands across several runs, or the validator's ordering check is shown to fire only on genuine out-of-order approvals.

case-sma-microscope-006.cue: an append-only record names a file path containing backslashes, and an escape sequence silently corrupts the path when the text is written through a shell or encoder
case-sma-microscope-006.lesson: Write paths in records with forward slashes or verified escaping, and read the written path back from disk before committing the record.
case-sma-microscope-006.falsification: Paths with backslashes round trip unchanged through the writing tool, so read-back verification never finds a corrupted path.

case-sma-microscope-007.cue: a plan's text describes what happens on a person's negative answer, while the executing code treats that answer as a failure and runs its abort path with side effects
case-sma-microscope-007.lesson: Make the operator distinguish a declined hold as a planned stop from an abort, and add a check that compares each plan's stated stop behavior against the code's actual events.
case-sma-microscope-007.falsification: Plan text and operator behavior are shown to agree on every decline path without any comparison, so the added comparison never catches a difference.

case-sma-microscope-008.cue: tests assert that nothing further runs after a planned stop, but never assert what the follow-on abort path sends, so a mutation harness cannot catch a wrong abort
case-sma-microscope-008.lesson: Add tests that assert the absence of each abort side effect after a planned stop, and confirm with a mutation that restoring the old behavior turns them red.
case-sma-microscope-008.falsification: The mutation harness catches wrong abort behavior without such explicit absence assertions, so the extra tests add no detection.

case-sma-microscope-009.cue: a bench experiment diverges from the simulation it was meant to confirm, and the person hints at a physical effect the simulation omits
case-sma-microscope-009.lesson: Rank candidate explanations in a diagnosis file, hold the result in the agent's own tree without handing it onward, and draft a separating measurement with its analysis declared before data.
case-sma-microscope-009.falsification: The top-ranked candidate is shown by the separating measurement to be irrelevant, or the discrepancy turns out to be a plain setup error that ranking would not have found.

case-sma-microscope-010.cue: a seat wants the form of an identifier and greps another agent's directory before checking the contract that declares it, crossing a read boundary no check can see
case-sma-microscope-010.lesson: Make the seat read the declaring contract first, and record every out-of-boundary read in the deviation log because no check can detect reads.
case-sma-microscope-010.falsification: A check that detects out-of-boundary reads is added, or seats never read beyond the contract anyway, making the confessional record unnecessary.

case-sma-microscope-011.cue: a build task is paused mid-way by a design decision that moves the layer it was changing, with no code written yet
case-sma-microscope-011.lesson: Record the stop with what was read, what is not done, the design so far and the open question, commit only that record, and start nothing new until the revised card lands.
case-sma-microscope-011.falsification: Paused work that leaves no such record is resumed just as fast and correctly by the next seat, so the written state adds nothing.

case-sma-bridge-001.cue: a long-running tool server loaded a contract pattern at start, a later commit updated the contract, and the running session refuses a call the committed contract allows
case-sma-bridge-001.lesson: Restart the server process after any contract change that it reads at import, and record the refused attempt, since connected does not mean current.
case-sma-bridge-001.falsification: The server reloads contract files on each call or on change, so a running session never refuses what the committed contract accepts.

case-sma-bridge-002.cue: a query log holds an answered line under a caller id that the seat did not make, and the server cannot verify who the caller is
case-sma-bridge-002.lesson: Treat the caller id in the query log as a claim rather than proof, add a server-session field to group lines, and report corroborated rather than verified results.
case-sma-bridge-002.falsification: The server gains real caller identity and attributes each line, so the id is verified and the weaker wording is no longer needed.

case-sma-bridge-003.cue: a needed check cannot be performed because the session has no connection to the required tool server, and the failure state could be mistaken for a refusal or stale code
case-sma-bridge-003.lesson: Name the failure state precisely as absent, with evidence from the connector status and the service's own log, and hand the fix to the person instead of spawning the server by hand.
case-sma-bridge-003.falsification: Windows reliably have the tools, or absent is indistinguishable in practice from the other states so naming it changes no action.

case-sma-bridge-004.cue: two separate sessions lack the same tool connection, which suggests a pattern in how the windows are launched rather than a one-off
case-sma-bridge-004.lesson: Record the repeat with the added evidence, label the root-cause guess as an untested hypothesis for the person to check, and list the tempting fixes that would break other rules.
case-sma-bridge-004.falsification: A window launched in the same way later has the tools, which refutes the guessed cause and shows the repeat was unrelated.

case-sma-bridge-005.cue: a failure list of states omits the working case, and an earlier prediction about the answer's shape is checked against a real run
case-sma-bridge-005.lesson: Add the success state to the task's list of states, read the actual answer instead of the prediction, and derive server freshness from version control and process start times.
case-sma-bridge-005.falsification: Seats reading the failure list alone still reach correct verdicts when the service works, so the extra state is unneeded.

case-sma-bridge-006.cue: a harness permission deny meant to be inert for tool paths resolves against a relative path extracted from a shell command and blocks part of a required delivery
case-sma-bridge-006.lesson: Exempt the inbox paths from the outward deny entries in the seat's settings, and do not route around the deny with another tool or path.
case-sma-bridge-006.falsification: Deny entries are shown never to match relative paths in shell commands, so the block came from another cause and the exemption changes nothing.

case-sma-incident-001.cue: a session-start hook or machine-level store feeds content from earlier closed projects into every session on the machine
case-sma-incident-001.lesson: Add a check that fails when any session hook or machine-level directory supplies content from outside the repository, and audit those locations whenever a project is closed.
case-sma-incident-001.falsification: Sessions started with such a hook present show no foreign terminology in their cards, so the leak never reached the design.

case-sma-incident-002.cue: a seat reviewing its own day finds errors at places it had marked as confirmed
case-sma-incident-002.lesson: Require the seat's instructions to mark a setting confirmed only with a cited observation from a run, and to write each known limit of a fix beside the fix.
case-sma-incident-002.falsification: Items marked confirmed without a cited observation prove as correct on re-check as items that cite one.

case-sma-incident-003.cue: a configuration fix is verified with an environment variable set by hand while real sessions leave it unset
case-sma-incident-003.lesson: Verify every configuration fix in a freshly started session with no hand-set variables, and record that run in the fix's verification step.
case-sma-incident-003.falsification: Fixes verified with hand-set variables behave identically in fresh sessions across many cases.

case-sma-incident-004.cue: a defect is fixed in one check while a sibling check or field of the same shape keeps it
case-sma-incident-004.lesson: When fixing a defect in a validator check, search all checks and schema fields for the same pattern and fix or list each one in the same commit.
case-sma-incident-004.falsification: Sweeps after such fixes repeatedly find no sibling carrying the same defect.

case-sma-incident-005.cue: a seat asserts from memory how many places a change must touch
case-sma-incident-005.lesson: Derive the list of sites to change from a search over the tree and put the search result in the commit message instead of an asserted count.
case-sma-incident-005.falsification: Counts asserted from memory match the search results across many changes.

case-sma-incident-006.cue: the handling of a schema field is fixed in one place while other places reading that field stay as they were
case-sma-incident-006.lesson: After changing how a field is handled, search every validator check and card schema that reads it and update them together in one commit.
case-sma-incident-006.falsification: The other places are shown not to depend on the changed behaviour, so fixing one place was enough.

case-sma-incident-007.cue: instructions state how many items are complete, a count read from prose rather than from a validator run
case-sma-incident-007.lesson: Produce counts in instructions from a validator run, and build a validator warning that flags a number in prose which disagrees with the cards on disk.
case-sma-incident-007.falsification: Counts written in prose stay equal to validator output over a long period even without any warning.

case-sma-incident-008.cue: instruction text claims a card or file is uncommitted or missing when the repository already holds it
case-sma-incident-008.lesson: Before writing a claim about repository state into instructions, read the commit history for it and cite the result beside the claim.
case-sma-incident-008.falsification: Claims about repository state written from prose prove as accurate as those checked against history.

case-sma-incident-009.cue: seats quote validator verdicts to each other without saying which tree the verdict judged
case-sma-incident-009.lesson: Keep the validator's last line naming the tree it judged, and require seats to quote that line together with any verdict they pass on.
case-sma-incident-009.falsification: Verdicts quoted without a tree name never mislead because committed and working states always agree.

case-sma-incident-010.cue: the same pinned query gets different answers from a server because its code changed between two session starts
case-sma-incident-010.lesson: Keep the check that compares logged answers to the same pinned query, and have the server write its build identity into every log entry.
case-sma-incident-010.falsification: Repeated pinned queries answered by different builds always give identical answers, so the comparison never fires.

case-sma-incident-011.cue: a seat reads a file across its session boundary, an act that leaves nothing for any check to find
case-sma-incident-011.lesson: Add to the seat's instructions a duty to declare any cross-boundary read in its notice, and restrict file access by permission where the tool allows it.
case-sma-incident-011.falsification: Audits of session transcripts find cross-boundary reads that no seat declared, showing declaration alone is not enough.

case-sma-incident-012.cue: a knowledge store returns nothing because it fails to recognise its own entries in the caller's wording
case-sma-incident-012.lesson: Add a validator check that replays every empty store result against the published table and flags those the store could have answered.
case-sma-incident-012.falsification: Replays of empty results never find an entry the store actually held.

case-sma-incident-013.cue: a role applies a grade ceiling to a number by inference without reading the plan row that already covers it
case-sma-incident-013.lesson: Require the architecture seat to cite the plan row or source naming a number's origin before ruling it a gap, and to ask the person when the origin is unknown.
case-sma-incident-013.falsification: Rulings made by inference without citing the plan match the person's answers when asked.

case-sma-incident-014.cue: seats debate options for a design question that the design record already answers
case-sma-incident-014.lesson: Require a design question to quote the searched plan section that bears on it before options are opened.
case-sma-incident-014.falsification: Debates opened without searching the record rarely turn out to be already settled by it.

case-sma-incident-015.cue: a commit-range validator run judges with the working copy's validator code, so one range gives different verdicts at different times
case-sma-incident-015.lesson: Make the validator's commit-range mode load its own code and contracts from the committed tree of that range, or state in the verdict line which code judged.
case-sma-incident-015.falsification: Commit-range verdicts stay identical when the working copy's validator differs from the committed one.

case-sma-incident-016.cue: a seat reverts a shared path with a checkout and discards another seat's uncommitted lines
case-sma-incident-016.lesson: Forbid checkout on shared paths in the seat's instructions, route reverts through a tool that refuses to drop lines the seat did not write, and save the worktree diff outside the tree first.
case-sma-incident-016.falsification: Reverts of shared paths never remove another seat's uncommitted lines even without such a tool.

case-sma-incident-017.cue: instructions name a fixture file that no commit holds and that cannot be found again
case-sma-incident-017.lesson: Add a validator check that every file named in instructions or in a check's description exists in the committed tree, and commit a fixture together with its check.
case-sma-incident-017.falsification: Every file named in instructions is found in the commit history, so the check would never fire.

case-sma-incident-018.cue: instructions assert how the tooling platform behaves, though nobody tested it
case-sma-incident-018.lesson: Test each platform-behaviour claim in a fresh session and cite the observed result before the claim enters the seat's instructions.
case-sma-incident-018.falsification: Platform-behaviour claims written from documentation alone prove right when tested.

case-sma-incident-019.cue: an untracked local settings file silently disables tools for several seats and no gate can see it
case-sma-incident-019.lesson: Add a commit-time or session hook that reports untracked local settings files holding deny entries, and have seats name such files in their notice.
case-sma-incident-019.falsification: Untracked local settings never differ in effect from tracked ones, and the hook's reports stay empty over a long time.

case-sma-incident-020.cue: an untracked settings file changes repeatedly while seats quote its contents to each other and nothing records the change
case-sma-incident-020.lesson: Have a hook write a hash of each untracked settings file to a log on disk at session start and at commit time so that changes become visible.
case-sma-incident-020.falsification: Untracked settings files never change during a working period, or nobody relies on their contents.

case-sma-incident-021.cue: a settings fix lands while sessions are running that read settings only at start
case-sma-incident-021.lesson: Require the hand-over notice for a settings fix to tell running seats to restart, and make a hook warn when a session began before the fix.
case-sma-incident-021.falsification: Running sessions pick up settings changes without a restart.

case-sma-incident-022.cue: a role is refused by a store access rule built to refuse it, and reads the refusal as a gap in the store
case-sma-incident-022.lesson: Make the store's refusal text state that the caller has no issued identity by design, and record the same line in the role's instructions.
case-sma-incident-022.falsification: Seats that receive the clarified refusal still file gaps for it.

case-sma-incident-023.cue: a seat testing server code behaviour is refused by an access rule meant for fact queries, and the line between the two is not written down
case-sma-incident-023.lesson: Write the line between measuring server behaviour and querying the store into the seat's instructions, and provide a test route that calls store functions directly.
case-sma-incident-023.falsification: Seats given the written line are still refused at the same rate.

case-sma-incident-024.cue: a seat verifying a colleague's measurement invents an identity that looks issued so it can pass an access gate
case-sma-incident-024.lesson: Have the server log every refused or unissued identity, and point verification work in the seat's instructions at direct store calls instead of the gated route.
case-sma-incident-024.falsification: Direct store calls and the gated route give different numbers, so direct calls are not a valid substitute for verification.

case-sma-incident-025.cue: instructions name a card field that does not exist in any schema while the enforcing mechanism works under another name
case-sma-incident-025.lesson: Add a validator check that every field name appearing in instructions exists in a schema file, and cite the schema beside it.
case-sma-incident-025.falsification: Misnamed fields in instructions never mislead anyone because the mechanism is enforced regardless of names.

case-sma-incident-026.cue: after an injecting hook and its mirrored content are removed, executable scripts that can rebuild the mirror remain
case-sma-incident-026.lesson: When removing an injection path, delete or disable the leftover scripts too, and add a check that machine-level directories hold nothing able to repopulate removed content.
case-sma-incident-026.falsification: Leftover scripts without a hook entry are never run by any session.

case-sma-incident-027.cue: a record is described as generated from another file, bound by a hash, while no generator exists
case-sma-incident-027.lesson: Add a validator check that any record declared generated has a generator in the tree and that its hash header matches the generator's output.
case-sma-incident-027.falsification: Records declared generated but edited by hand stay consistent with their source without any generator.

case-sma-incident-028.cue: a settled question is corrected in some table rows of the plan while other rows still cite it as open
case-sma-incident-028.lesson: When correcting one plan row for a settled question, search all sections for rows citing that question and correct them in the same commit.
case-sma-incident-028.falsification: Sibling rows citing a settled question are never found stale after a correction.

case-sma-incident-029.cue: a section of the plan is corrected while other sections still describe the old arrangement
case-sma-incident-029.lesson: When correcting how the plan describes a record or language rule, search every section for the old description and fix all hits in one commit.
case-sma-incident-029.falsification: Other sections never repeat the old description after a single-section correction.

case-sma-incident-030.cue: a seat fixes a counting error in a check and later makes the same kind of counting error again
case-sma-incident-030.lesson: When fixing a counting error in a check, add a fixture for each distinct way of miscounting, such as a grade string counted as an entry, in the same commit.
case-sma-incident-030.falsification: Counting errors recur in checks that already hold a fixture for every miscount.

case-sma-incident-031.cue: a refusal is keyed to lift when schema fields are declared while the code that would write the refused content is gone
case-sma-incident-031.lesson: Require the replacement code to land beside any refusal that lifts on a schema change, reading the same schema, with a fixture that stays refused until the content exists.
case-sma-incident-031.falsification: Lifting such a refusal on declaration alone never lets an incomplete card out.

case-sma-incident-032.cue: a naming rule is enforced by a check while the hazard behind it, a lookup returning the wrong substance, passes silently
case-sma-incident-032.lesson: Keep the naming check and add a check or fixture comparing a retrieved quantity's material or medium to the card's subject before an axis computes from it.
case-sma-incident-032.falsification: Queries that obey the naming rule never return entries for the wrong substance.

case-sma-incident-033.cue: a hand-over practice such as naming the intended seat on each task card lapses with nothing recording it
case-sma-incident-033.lesson: Make the task-card schema require the seat field and have the validator reject cards that lack it.
case-sma-incident-033.falsification: Cards that lack the seat field cause no mis-delivery.

case-sma-incident-034.cue: two seats write the same path and a pathspec commit takes the worktree state, so one seat commits the other's overwrite as its own
case-sma-incident-034.lesson: Build the commit tool to refuse any named path whose content was last written by another seat, and keep pathspec commits out of the seats' practice.
case-sma-incident-034.falsification: Two seats writing one path never produce a commit that carries the other's content.

case-sma-incident-035.cue: a seat reads a file at a path shared with another seat and reports its content as the recipient's
case-sma-incident-035.lesson: Give each task card a distinct output path per seat and have the validator reject cards that share a goal path.
case-sma-incident-035.falsification: Seats sharing a goal path never report each other's file content as their own.

case-sma-incident-036.cue: a projection of a store entry omits fields that carry conflicts or refutations, losing information about an answer
case-sma-incident-036.lesson: Add a check that every field of a store entry appears in the projection returned to callers or is listed as intentionally dropped.
case-sma-incident-036.falsification: Dropped fields never change an answer's meaning for any caller.

case-sma-incident-037.cue: a projection of a store entry omits descriptive fields such as kind, symbol, unit or validity, losing information about an answer
case-sma-incident-037.lesson: Extend the projection check so that each descriptive field of a store entry is carried or explicitly listed as dropped, with a fixture holding all of them.
case-sma-incident-037.falsification: Callers never need the omitted descriptive fields to read an answer correctly.

case-sma-incident-038.cue: a check derives a grade from a source field at one layer of an entry while the same field also exists in a nested layer nothing looks into
case-sma-incident-038.lesson: Make the grade check read the source at every layer that carries it, with a fixture where the layers differ.
case-sma-incident-038.falsification: Entry-level and nested sources always agree, so reading one layer gives the same grade.

case-sma-incident-039.cue: a card schema written with one kind of producer in mind has no slot for another kind to state what it read
case-sma-incident-039.lesson: Before freezing a card schema, draft a first card for every producer kind and add fields or alternatives wherever a card cannot be written.
case-sma-incident-039.falsification: First cards for new producer kinds fit the schema without change.

case-sma-incident-040.cue: one field name serves two meanings in a contract because only one producer side existed when it was named
case-sma-incident-040.lesson: Give each distinct meaning its own field name in the schema, and add a check that rejects a name used with two meanings.
case-sma-incident-040.falsification: A single name used for two meanings never leads to a wrong card.

case-sma-incident-041.cue: a contract field offers alignment options that all assume hardware, leaving a producer without a clock no valid choice
