case-sma-incident-041.lesson: Add to the contract field an explicit option for producers without a clock, with a required reason, and draft a card from such a producer to test it.
case-sma-incident-041.falsification: Producers without a clock always find a valid option among the existing ones.

case-sma-incident-042.cue: a count read off a validator run mixes example fixtures with real cards from agent trees
case-sma-incident-042.lesson: Make the validator report fixtures separately from cards in agent trees, and require any reported count to name the tree it covers.
case-sma-incident-042.falsification: Fixture and real card totals never differ in practice, so a mixed count misleads nobody.

case-sma-incident-043.cue: a rule's effect can be seen only by trying the denied operation, while the check audits only how the rule is spelled
case-sma-incident-043.lesson: Add a probe that attempts the denied operation in a scratch context and expects refusal, next to the spelling audit.
case-sma-incident-043.falsification: The spelling audit agrees with probe outcomes for every rule.

case-sma-incident-044.cue: a seat reads across a session boundary and quotes the rule's own self-test while failing it, visible only because the seat said so
case-sma-incident-044.lesson: Require the seat to run the rule's self-test on its own work before quoting it, and to declare cross-boundary reads in its notice.
case-sma-incident-044.falsification: Seats quoting a rule's self-test without running it never fail that test.

case-sma-incident-045.cue: a registry or contract file states a tool behaviour that is wrong, with no failure to reveal it
case-sma-incident-045.lesson: Test each tool-behaviour claim in a scratch repository before it enters a registry file and record the test beside the claim.
case-sma-incident-045.falsification: Tool-behaviour claims written without testing are right as often as tested ones.

case-sma-incident-046.cue: a check demands exact reproduction of a planned value while the instrument quantises it, and wrongly fails a valid fixture
case-sma-incident-046.lesson: Give the plan card a declared tolerance or quantisation field that the check reads, and add fixtures for quantised values in both directions.
case-sma-incident-046.falsification: Exact reproduction of planned values holds for every instrument, so no tolerance is needed.

case-sma-incident-047.cue: a seat finds several statements a contract makes that have no field to hold them
case-sma-incident-047.lesson: Give each unplaced statement a schema field, or record it as a declared unknown with a task, instead of leaving it in prose.
case-sma-incident-047.falsification: Statements left without a slot never block a card or change a result.

case-sma-incident-048.cue: a rule inside a check is switched off and the expected-failure totals do not change because the rule has no fixture
case-sma-incident-048.lesson: Require every rule in a check to carry a rejected fixture that fails when that rule is off, and keep the expect-fail totals strict.
case-sma-incident-048.falsification: Rules without a fixture are switched off and the totals still change, so fixtures add nothing.

case-sma-incident-049.cue: a local git configuration outside any tree overrides the identity a seat commits with, so a path check refuses it repeatedly
case-sma-incident-049.lesson: Keep the commit-time identity warning, and have the commit tool set the committer identity through environment variables so that configuration cannot override it.
case-sma-incident-049.falsification: Seats using configuration flags are never overridden by local configuration files.

case-sma-incident-050.cue: a commit hook refuses with a generic line that does not name its cause
case-sma-incident-050.lesson: Make the pre-commit hook print a FAIL line naming the cause on every nonzero exit path.
case-sma-incident-050.falsification: Hook refusals without a named cause are diagnosed as quickly as those that name one.

case-sma-incident-051.cue: a seat amends a commit with no paths and the rebuild takes another seat's staged files from the shared index
case-sma-incident-051.lesson: Make the commit tool refuse a pathless amend and refuse any amend while the shared index holds paths from another seat.
case-sma-incident-051.falsification: Pathless amends never pick up another seat's staged files.

case-sma-incident-052.cue: head moves between a seat's check of the index and its amend, so the amend rewrites another session's commit
case-sma-incident-052.lesson: Have the commit tool verify that head is unchanged between its check and the amend, or forbid amend and make every correction a new commit.
case-sma-incident-052.falsification: Head never moves between a check and an amend in the shared folder.

case-sma-incident-053.cue: a commit whose message is built from inline shell substitution silently produces no commit
case-sma-incident-053.lesson: Have the commit tool take its message from a file path and confirm after the run that head moved to a new commit.
case-sma-incident-053.falsification: Inline substitution messages never leave a commit unmade.

case-sma-incident-054.cue: the same silent no-commit failure recurs after it was noted once, again triggering an amend as recovery
case-sma-incident-054.lesson: Make the commit tool exit nonzero whenever head did not move, and say in the seat's instructions that no commit exists until the tool confirms it.
case-sma-incident-054.falsification: The failure never recurs once it is documented, even without a tool check.

case-sma-incident-055.cue: a commit fails on a lock held by another seat while the seat's filtered output hides the error
case-sma-incident-055.lesson: Have the commit tool report any git fatal output and forbid filtering its output to failure lines only, confirming that head moved.
case-sma-incident-055.falsification: Filtered output never hides a failed commit because git always reports through the filtered lines.

case-sma-incident-056.cue: prescribed pre-commit diff compares against the shared index while the commit is built from head, so it hides a colleague's staged lines
case-sma-incident-056.lesson: Have the commit tool show the diff of the named paths against head, and keep the instructions prescribing the head form.
case-sma-incident-056.falsification: A diff against the shared index shows exactly the lines the commit carries.

case-sma-incident-057.cue: a stale shared index makes a diff show lines that would not land and a colleague is stopped needlessly
case-sma-incident-057.lesson: Have the commit tool diff against head and list other seats' staged paths before reporting what would land.
case-sma-incident-057.falsification: A stale shared index never changes what a diff shows.

case-sma-incident-058.cue: an identity copied out of a delivered message carries a substituted character and matches no registry entry
case-sma-incident-058.lesson: Have the commit tool take identity only from the seat registry and reject non-ASCII characters in identity strings.
case-sma-incident-058.falsification: Delivered messages arrive with identical characters, so copied identities always match.

case-sma-incident-059.cue: a hook added to warn seats about a setting reaches only sessions started afterwards, not the seats it was written for
case-sma-incident-059.lesson: Place the warning in the commit hook, which runs when the identity is spent, rather than in a session-start hook.
case-sma-incident-059.falsification: Session-start warnings reach already running seats.

case-sma-incident-060.cue: a server's refusal recorder keeps keyword arguments while its tools are called positionally, so refusals lose what was asked
case-sma-incident-060.lesson: Keep the server self-test assertion that calls each tool in the positional form and checks the recorded fields, and see it fail on old code first.
case-sma-incident-060.falsification: Recorders written for keyword arguments log positional calls completely.

case-sma-incident-061.cue: a script or launcher picks an interpreter by name on a machine whose platform supplies a same-named stub that is not the real tool
case-sma-incident-061.lesson: Make the launcher and every repository script choose an interpreter by running a probe of it, never by looking up its name.
case-sma-incident-061.falsification: A name-only lookup picks a working interpreter on every machine in use, with no probe ever rejecting a candidate.

case-sma-incident-062.cue: the validator and hooks, written on one operating system, print paths or totals in a form that breaks them on another machine
case-sma-incident-062.lesson: Make the validator and hooks print paths with forward slashes and print complete totals, and run them on every operating system in use.
case-sma-incident-062.falsification: Runs on every operating system in use give identical output and verdicts without any path or total formatting change.

case-sma-incident-063.cue: a checker depends on the caller's default text encoding, so checks crash on a machine whose shell default differs
case-sma-incident-063.lesson: Make the validator re-run itself in its text-encoding mode when that mode is not already set, so no check depends on the caller's environment.
case-sma-incident-063.falsification: A run without the environment setting finishes every check on the other platform with no decode error and without the self re-run.

case-sma-incident-064.cue: a claim that no environment setting is needed rests on a test whose shell silently inherited that setting from a settings file
case-sma-incident-064.lesson: Run any test of an environment-dependent claim in a shell where the variable is explicitly unset, and let the instructions state only claims so tested.
case-sma-incident-064.falsification: The harness settings block never changes a test result compared with a clean shell across the claims tested this way.

case-sma-incident-065.cue: a server is launched through a shell or helper that is not on the application's own search path on some machine
case-sma-incident-065.lesson: Make the bootstrap check confirm that every program a launch entry calls resolves under the application's own search path, and report the missing one by name.
case-sma-incident-065.falsification: Every launch entry starts on every machine with no search path change, so the bootstrap check never reports a missing program.

case-sma-incident-066.cue: a validator walks the whole tree and one unreadable entry from another platform's tooling crashes it for every seat
case-sma-incident-066.lesson: Make the validator prune skipped directories before touching any path, and report an unreadable entry elsewhere as a named failing check.
case-sma-incident-066.falsification: A tree holding an unreadable entry inside a skipped directory validates cleanly under the older touch-first order, so the order never mattered.

case-sma-incident-067.cue: a launcher accepts a bare interpreter that exists but lacks the packages the server imports
case-sma-incident-067.lesson: Make the launcher's interpreter probe import the modules the server needs, so an interpreter is chosen only if it can actually run the server.
case-sma-incident-067.falsification: A bare interpreter lacking the required modules is never the first match on any machine in use, so an existence-only probe would do.

case-sma-incident-068.cue: a second independent cause of the same tool outage stays hidden behind the first fix, here a search path differing between machine and user scope
case-sma-incident-068.lesson: Make the bootstrap check test each launch dependency under the application's own search path, separating machine and user entries, and record the remedy per machine.
case-sma-incident-068.falsification: The application's search path always equals the shell's, so a shell-side check predicts the application's behaviour on every machine.

case-sma-incident-069.cue: instructions describe a failure as current after a configuration fix has already made it stale, and another seat acts on that reading
case-sma-incident-069.lesson: Make the instructions state any outage claim together with the log line or commit it rests on and its time, so a reader can compare it with later evidence.
case-sma-incident-069.falsification: Outage claims in instructions are always rewritten before any session reads them, so no reader acts on a stale one.

case-sma-incident-070.cue: a commit tool builds its tree from the head it read, then waits on a lock while another seat's commit lands on the branch
case-sma-incident-070.lesson: Make the commit tool rebuild its tree from the current head after any lock wait and run the gate again before writing the commit.
case-sma-incident-070.falsification: The branch head never moves during lock waits in practice, or a frozen-tree commit never reverts another seat's work.

case-sma-incident-071.cue: a private-index commit moves the branch head but leaves the shared index entry for the committed path unchanged
case-sma-incident-071.lesson: Make the commit tool move the shared index entry of every committed path to the new commit once it lands.
case-sma-incident-071.falsification: A plain commit made right after the tool's commit never carries a reversal of the tool's committed change, even without that index step.

case-sma-incident-072.cue: instructions give a count of files or lines with no method, matching no run, and readers take it as measured
case-sma-incident-072.lesson: Add a validator warning for counts in prose that name no command, run or card, so each count must cite how it was read.
case-sma-incident-072.falsification: Method-less counts in prose match a fresh run whenever checked, so the warning would only add noise.

case-sma-incident-073.cue: seats re-perform a fragile multi-step commit procedure from prose and one of them loses the commit to a lock race
case-sma-incident-073.lesson: Make the commit tool own lock waiting and retrying so no seat repeats the procedure by hand from prose.
case-sma-incident-073.falsification: Seats following the prose procedure never lose a commit to a lock race over a long window.

case-sma-incident-074.cue: a commit made by plumbing commands skips the pre-commit gate, so only a later hook or manual run can judge it
case-sma-incident-074.lesson: Keep the pre-push hook judging every pushed range and make the commit message name what judged a plumbing commit instead of the gate.
case-sma-incident-074.falsification: A plumbing commit reaches the shared branch with no later gate judging it, or plumbing commits stop occurring.

case-sma-incident-075.cue: a launcher fix is verified in a developer shell that has a tool the application's own environment lacks
case-sma-incident-075.lesson: Run launcher tests under the application's own search path and environment, and record which environment each test used.
case-sma-incident-075.falsification: Results from the developer shell and from the application's own environment never differ for any launcher test.

case-sma-incident-076.cue: two validator runs with different verdicts are compared as if only the interpreter changed, while another seat's edit moved the judged tree
case-sma-incident-076.lesson: Keep the validator's last line naming the judged tree, including uncommitted paths, and compare verdicts only between runs with the same line.
case-sma-incident-076.falsification: Two runs with the same judged-tree line give different verdicts, showing the line does not capture what moves the result.

case-sma-incident-077.cue: bare commands fail in every session because of a file the harness itself writes outside any repository tree, and a seat reads it as a broken machine
case-sma-incident-077.lesson: Add to the seat's instructions that a bare command failing where its absolute binary works points first to harness-written shell files, not the machine.
case-sma-incident-077.falsification: Bare commands never fail where the absolute binary works because of harness-written shell files.

case-sma-incident-078.cue: instructions claim that nothing records some fact, though the logs already carry it
case-sma-incident-078.lesson: Require a search of the logs for the fact, cited in the commit message, before instructions may state that nothing records it.
case-sma-incident-078.falsification: Absence claims written into instructions without a search turn out right every time.

case-sma-incident-079.cue: a measured count is presented as settling more than its question can see
case-sma-incident-079.lesson: State beside each such count in the instructions the exact question it answers and what it cannot see.
case-sma-incident-079.falsification: Readers never draw a broader conclusion from such counts than the stated question supports.

case-sma-incident-080.cue: a seat checks whether a method is sound but not whether running it is within its role
case-sma-incident-080.lesson: Add to the seat's instructions a first step of checking the operation against the seat's registered role before judging the method.
case-sma-incident-080.falsification: Seats that check only soundness never run an operation outside their role.

case-sma-incident-081.cue: a plan paragraph states that something cannot be done, true when written, and stays after it becomes false
case-sma-incident-081.lesson: Add a check that fails plan prose making a negative capability claim without a pointer to the card or run it rests on.
case-sma-incident-081.falsification: Negative capability claims in the plan are corrected quickly enough that no reader ever relies on a stale one.

case-sma-incident-082.cue: a new class of case enters a plan section and nobody names it, so no vocabulary entry or schema slot exists for it
case-sma-incident-082.lesson: Require that a commit adding the first case of a new class also adds its entry to the class vocabulary, checked by the validator.
case-sma-incident-082.falsification: First cases of new classes are always named later with no loss, so same-commit naming adds nothing.

case-sma-incident-083.cue: a knowledge entry states its validity conditions as a free sentence that no check or reader can act on
case-sma-incident-083.lesson: Make the knowledge-entry schema hold validity conditions as structured fields and reject an entry whose conditions exist only as prose.
case-sma-incident-083.falsification: Free-sentence validity conditions are read and acted on correctly by sessions or checks without structure.

case-sma-incident-084.cue: a field is filled but its content is inconsistent with a sibling field, and the check looks only at presence
case-sma-incident-084.lesson: Make the validator check a filled expiry or horizon against the event field it depends on, rejecting a horizon with no triggering event.
case-sma-incident-084.falsification: A horizon filled beside an empty event never leads to a wrong decision or stale entry.

case-sma-incident-085.cue: a reference field is present but resolves to nothing, and the presence check passes it
case-sma-incident-085.lesson: Make the validator resolve every task reference to an existing task file instead of only checking that the field is filled.
case-sma-incident-085.falsification: References that fail to resolve never occur over a long window, so presence checks suffice.

case-sma-incident-086.cue: a registry row keeps a path after the file was removed, and nothing checks the path still exists
case-sma-incident-086.lesson: Make the validator check that every path in a seat's registry row exists or matches a declared pattern, and fail on a stale one.
case-sma-incident-086.falsification: Stale paths in registry rows never affect any check or any seat's boundary.

case-sma-incident-087.cue: a flag is carried beside a number that contradicts it, and no check compares them
case-sma-incident-087.lesson: Make the validator compare a met flag with the number and threshold it sits beside, failing on contradiction.
case-sma-incident-087.falsification: Flag and number contradictions never lead to a wrong conclusion or accepted card.

case-sma-incident-088.cue: a tool reports the outcome of its own attempt, which is true of that attempt but false of the state a seat will act on
case-sma-incident-088.lesson: Make the commit tool read the remote state after a refused push and report whether the commit is published, not only what its own push did.
case-sma-incident-088.falsification: A refused push report always matches the remote state read afterwards, even without the read-back.

case-sma-incident-089.cue: prose cites another file by bare line number although that file is edited often by several seats
case-sma-incident-089.lesson: Keep the schema pattern that requires each prose reference to name the commit it was read at, enforced by a check.
case-sma-incident-089.falsification: Referenced files never change between citation and reading, so bare line numbers stay valid.

case-sma-incident-090.cue: a seat commits around the commit tool right after the instructions began requiring it, and nothing tells it at that moment
case-sma-incident-090.lesson: Make the pre-commit hook warn a seat identity at commit time when the commit was not made through the commit tool.
case-sma-incident-090.falsification: Seats use the tool every time without any reminder, so commits around it do not occur.

case-sma-incident-091.cue: a seat tells another seat what a tool does, inferred from similar commands and never run
case-sma-incident-091.lesson: Add to the seat's instructions that a claim about a tool's behaviour must cite a run in a scratch clone before it is sent.
case-sma-incident-091.falsification: Inferred claims about tool behaviour are as accurate as measured ones, so the extra run adds nothing.

case-sma-incident-092.cue: a commit lands without the commit tool and leaves no line in the tool's own log
case-sma-incident-092.lesson: Keep the pre-commit warning and have the periodic harness pass count first-parent commits missing from the tool's log.
case-sma-incident-092.falsification: Commits missing from the tool's log stop occurring after the warning, so the periodic count shows none.

case-sma-incident-093.cue: a rejected fixture's verdict depends on live state that a person may change, so the gate refuses every commit with the fixture untouched
case-sma-incident-093.lesson: Make every rejected fixture group read only its own configuration, never the live person-written values, in every check that reads them.
case-sma-incident-093.falsification: A fixture's verdict stays the same when the live person-written values change, so isolation is unneeded.

case-sma-incident-094.cue: an example or fixture holds a time bound that the wall clock will pass, so the gate begins refusing every commit without warning
case-sma-incident-094.lesson: Write fixtures with time bounds already past or far away, and have the harness pass list example expiry dates nearest first.
case-sma-incident-094.falsification: An example's time bound passes the clock with no gate refusal, so expiry never matters.

case-sma-incident-095.cue: a session drafts a horizon or limit number into a plan that the rules reserve for the person to choose
case-sma-incident-095.lesson: Add a check or review step that fails plan text holding a numeric limit not traced to the person's recorded word.
case-sma-incident-095.falsification: Seat-drafted numeric limits without a person source never appear in plan drafts.

case-sma-incident-096.cue: a gate compares the tree with the branch head as it stands during the run, and another seat's commit lands meanwhile
case-sma-incident-096.lesson: Make the commit tool treat a gate refusal as a verdict only when the head is unchanged since the tree was built, and otherwise rebuild and judge again.
case-sma-incident-096.falsification: Gate refusals under a moved head always remain true for the rebuilt tree.

case-sma-incident-097.cue: a path is meant to be written by one seat, but only that seat's own boundary narrows and other seats' boundaries still include it
case-sma-incident-097.lesson: Make the validator check that a path reserved to one seat is excluded from every other seat's registered paths.
case-sma-incident-097.falsification: No other seat ever commits to the reserved path, so exclusion adds no protection.

case-sma-incident-098.cue: two sessions draft the same design question because work is divided by window and nothing in the tree marks a question as taken
case-sma-incident-098.lesson: Add a tree-visible claim record for open design questions that a session must write before drafting, read through the task queue.
case-sma-incident-098.falsification: Parallel sessions never draft the same question even with no claim record.

case-sma-incident-099.cue: a tool asks for confirmation of a list that the caller already approved through a flag passed on the invocation itself
case-sma-incident-099.lesson: Make the commit tool refuse to publish other seats' commits unless a confirmation is given after the list is shown, never through an invocation flag.
case-sma-incident-099.falsification: Pushes with a pre-passed flag never publish another seat's work against the person's wishes.

case-sma-incident-100.cue: a retry limit nobody chose refuses correct work when the shared branch moves more often than expected
case-sma-incident-100.lesson: Make the commit tool log the number of head moves per attempt so the person can choose the limit from the distribution.
case-sma-incident-100.falsification: Refusals at the limit never recur over a long window, so the distribution is not needed.

case-sma-incident-101.cue: the same seat is refused again at a retry limit after a long lock wait, with the gate passing each time
case-sma-incident-101.lesson: Make the commit tool log lock wait time beside rebuild count so the person can see whether waits drive refusals at the limit.
case-sma-incident-101.falsification: Refusals at the limit do not correlate with lock wait time.

case-sma-incident-102.cue: a seat hits a person-owned limit and must choose between raising it and rerunning with the default
case-sma-incident-102.lesson: Keep the commit tool's limit a person-owned setting, and have seats rerun at the default while the tool logs each refusal for counting.
case-sma-incident-102.falsification: Seats raising the limit themselves cause no harm and no disagreement with the person.

case-sma-incident-103.cue: a schema refuses to record a proposal until the person's word exists, but the proposal must exist to ask the person
case-sma-incident-103.lesson: Make the proposal schema accept a loosening proposal in a pending-person-word state, while the landing check still refuses landing without the word.
case-sma-incident-103.falsification: Loosening questions are always asked and answered without a proposal record, so the pending state is unused.

case-sma-incident-104.cue: output from a discarded attempt prints failure lines in the same form as a real refusal, ahead of a successful rebuild
case-sma-incident-104.lesson: Make the commit tool label every line from a discarded run as discarded, or drop those lines from the output.
case-sma-incident-104.falsification: Readers never mistake discarded-run lines for a verdict, even when they are printed unlabelled.

case-sma-incident-105.cue: a reader filters tool output for a failure word and sees a discarded attempt's line without its framing
case-sma-incident-105.lesson: Make the commit tool end its output with one verdict line stating committed or refused, so that filtering for the failure word is not needed.
case-sma-incident-105.falsification: Filtering output for failure lines never gives a wrong reading of a commit's outcome.

case-sma-incident-106.cue: a command denial guards one shell tool while a second shell tool on the same machine runs the same text
case-sma-incident-106.lesson: Make the validator check that every command denial in a settings file has a twin for each shell tool available on the machine.
case-sma-incident-106.falsification: A denial written for one shell tool also refuses the same text through the other shell tool.

case-sma-incident-107.cue: instructions state a settings timing rule as general, but one observation shows a running session picked up an edit
case-sma-incident-107.lesson: Qualify the instruction sentence about when settings are read with the observation and what remains unmeasured, until a second measurement.
case-sma-incident-107.falsification: A running session never picks up edited settings without a restart, in repeated trials.

case-sma-incident-108.cue: an intent-to-add entry in the shared index survives a tool commit and reads as a staged deletion after the head moves
case-sma-incident-108.lesson: Keep the commit tool moving intent-to-add entries of committed paths to the new commit, with its fixture.
case-sma-incident-108.falsification: A plain commit after a tool commit with intent-to-add entries never deletes the committed files.

case-sma-incident-109.cue: a command pattern meant to block running also blocks reads that merely name the guarded word
case-sma-incident-109.lesson: Keep the dedicated read, search and glob tools guaranteed open, and have seats use them when a command pattern over-blocks instead of rewording the command.
case-sma-incident-109.falsification: A seat needs a read that only a blocked command could perform.

case-sma-incident-110.cue: two seats with identical paths on different computers write date-keyed records into the same append-only files
case-sma-incident-110.lesson: Make record ids and file names carry the machine tag so two seats on the same paths cannot collide, and keep the duplicate refusal at the gate.
case-sma-incident-110.falsification: Two seats on the same paths work on the same day with date-only keys and never collide.

case-sma-incident-111.cue: a periodic duty belongs to a seat that acts only when a message reaches it, so days pass without the duty running
case-sma-incident-111.lesson: Have the person decide on a standing scheduler for the periodic pass, since nothing in the harness wakes the seat.
case-sma-incident-111.falsification: The pass runs on every due day with no scheduler, driven only by other seats' messages.

case-sma-incident-112.cue: a commit under the person's default identity sweeps in several seats' unfinished work outside the commit tool
case-sma-incident-112.lesson: Make the pre-commit hook warn when the committer is not a registered seat and the staged paths belong to a seat's declared work.
case-sma-incident-112.falsification: Commits under a non-seat identity never carry a seat's unfinished work.

case-sma-incident-113.cue: a pattern is widened in one schema although copies of it sit in other schemas that cite the same identifiers
case-sma-incident-113.lesson: Change every schema copy of a shared pattern in the same commit, and add a check that fails when copies of one pattern differ.
case-sma-incident-113.falsification: Copies of a pattern in different schemas never diverge in a way a check would catch.

case-sma-incident-114.cue: a check returns not-applicable when the tree holds no cards, so a run over other artifact kinds alone judges nothing
case-sma-incident-114.lesson: Make the validator schema-check harness artifacts even when no cards exist, reporting not-applicable only when nothing of that kind is present.
case-sma-incident-114.falsification: A run over harness artifacts alone gives the same verdict as a full run in every case.

case-sma-incident-115.cue: the person grants permission through a new channel, but the record schema holds the person's word in one form only
case-sma-incident-115.lesson: Extend the person-word schema in the harness records with a console-signed form before that channel is used, so the landing check can accept it.
case-sma-incident-115.falsification: Permissions given through the new channel are never used, so the schema never needs the form.

case-sma-incident-116.cue: a check judges every old record against a working-copy file read at run time, so a missing or changed file fails old correct lines
case-sma-incident-116.lesson: Make the check judge each ledger line against the file as committed at that line's landing commit, not the working copy file.
case-sma-incident-116.falsification: The working copy file stays present and unchanged on every computer, so old lines always pass.

case-sma-incident-117.cue: a daily duty goes unrun for several days because its seat acts only when woken, and the question of scheduling stays open
case-sma-incident-117.lesson: Make each retro name the gap between its date and the last pass record, so missed days are visible when the pass finally runs.
case-sma-incident-117.falsification: Gaps between pass records never occur, so the retro's gap line would always be empty.

case-sma-incident-118.cue: a person-owned retry limit refuses a large correct commit that passes on a later attempt
case-sma-incident-118.lesson: Make the commit tool report to the person each pass the rate of attempts reaching the limit, with the head-move distribution.
case-sma-incident-118.falsification: Attempts reaching the limit stay absent as the number of seats and commits grows.

case-sma-incident-119.cue: a boundary check attributes to a merging seat paths that git merged cleanly from both sides, so clean merges are refused
case-sma-incident-119.lesson: Keep the validator reading a merge's own paths from its combined-diff patch, with fixtures for a clean merge and a merge adding its own change.
case-sma-incident-119.falsification: A clean merge of another computer's work is refused for paths the merging seat never wrote.
